newsitem.title: USA: Nearby CME lumber futures end with limit gains.
newsitem.headline: Nearby CME lumber futures end with limit gains.

text.p: CME lumber futures closed with limit gains in January and March contracts in reaction to higher cash lumber prices, active home sales, and a severe snowstorm in the Pacific Northwest, traders and analysts said.
The pools of remaining limit bids were small in both January and March, traders said.

Traders said talk of spruce trading from $400 to $405 per tbf Monday and of possible extended shutdowns at Pacific Northwest sawmills because of the blizzard there fueled buying in the futures. Also, a 1.8 percent jump in existing home sales in November to 4.04 million units, according to the National Association of Realtors, was seen as bullish.
Lumber closed up $10.00 to down $3.20 with January up the limit at $414.70 and March up the limit at $407.30.
